-    Why Apple, why this role

-    Example on partnership, colloboration, challenging decisions

-    Technical problem you solved
-    Best accomplishment
-     Executive summary, one hypothetical case question on priority and rollout
-    Failure/mistake made
-    How do you ramp-up in new domain

2 Technical rounds (with 2 eng managers each)

As a candidate for an open position, generally only one side knows what they are willing to pay somebody in the role and it's usually not the candidate. I'll provide a different perspective: Recruiters ask this question to assess whether the candidate will even "fit" into their range. Most recruiters don't ask for this, but some do. Employers these days (at least in CA) provide pay transparency and disclose pay range up front in job postings. If the candidate's expectation is beyond what's advertised, the recruiter will probably not want to move forward since they'd be wasting time. At the very least they want to know if you are "ok" with that range and there's alignment.
